text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- President Sali Berisha has declared the Gjallica company is bankrupt, and its director Fitim Gerxhalliu has been arrested. It ran a investment scheme paying 11 percent a month.

- Gjallica director Gerxhalliu has admitted there is no money to pay creditors but denied the firm had gone bankrupt. The paper alleges television said the firm had gone bankrupt to avoid investors massing at its offices in Vlore.
- About 210,000 investors in the frozen Xhaferri scheme will receive 52 percent of the sums they have invested. They were promised 200 percent monthly interest.
- A petition by 900,000 creditors of the fallen Gjallica firm demands president Sali Berisha sell a big power dam in northern Albania to pay them back or resign.
- The paper published a blank page for the second day protesting against the arrest of its correspondent Roland Beqiraj nine days ago.
- President Berisha has blamed people for investing in pyramid schemes and has told investment companies who also run high interest schemes to cut wages and refrain from luxuries.
- The Forum for Democracy has demanded the resignation of the government because its economic policy has failed, regardless of whether it can return money from pyramid schemes.
- Michel Barnier, French Minister for European Affairs has cancelled his visit to Tirana because of the tense situation in Albania.
- Transport in Albania's biggest port of Durres has been paralysed by a strike of drivers demanding increased wages.
- Police and the army are patrolling the streets of the southern town of Vlore fearing gatherings from investors in the failed scheme Gjallica.
- The Republican Party says a round table chaired by President Sali Berisha left them no wiser and completely surrounded by fog on the collapse of pyramid schemes.
- Shemsie Kadria, co-owner of the Gjallica scheme, has declared she does not recognise debts incurred by the firm, saying it is a matter for director Fitim Gerxhalliu.
- Berisha blames the opposition for manipulating evil-doing elements for their political ends.
